title: Push platform guide: urgency mapping for broadcast mentions
description:
Update jmap-push-platform-guide.md (and possibly jmap-chat-push-platform-guide.md) with platform-specific urgency mapping for the new broadcast-scope mention types.

Blocked on jmap-chat-spec-fig9.2 (main draft) and jmap-chat-spec-fig9.4 (push draft) for the field shape.

Scope:
- For each push platform (APNs, FCM, WebPush, etc.) covered by the platform guide, document what urgency level / interruption-level / priority value to use for each broadcast scope
- Document any platform-specific badging / sound / banner recommendations
- Document how clients should locally interpret per-scope flags for their own UI (this is non-normative implementer guidance, not spec text)

The guide files are non-normative; they describe deployment practice. RFC 2119 keywords are not used here.

Note: this bead was originally created in the same parallel batch as fig9.3 and fig9.4 but lost an ID race; it is the third Epic A implementation child after the federation and push draft beads. The fig9.3/fig9.4 swap (fig9.3=federation, fig9.4=push, opposite of what the description text in those beads says about being created "third" or "second") is cosmetic — the dependency graph is correct in both.
acceptance_criteria:
- Per-platform urgency mapping documented for `@everyone`, `@here`, `@admins`
- Clients are given guidance on banner/sound/badge handling per scope
- Non-normative tone preserved (no MUST/SHOULD/MAY)
- Cross-references to the push draft fields are correct
close_reason: Updated §Urgency trigger to mentionScopes; added §Per-scope urgency recommendations table covering @everyone/@here/@admins/@user; added §Client UI interpretation per-scope rendering guidance with forward-compat rule for unknown scopes; updated truncation no-drop list. Per-platform urgency translation continues to flow through the general jmap-push-platform-guide.md (no per-platform per-scope tables added because the chat-specific recommendation is platform-agnostic 'high'; platform translation of 'high' is already documented).
